subject: arts-music
unit_title: Advanced Studio Practice and Personal Direction
lesson_title: Concept model A: advanced composition and visual hierarchy
objective_constraints: Two placement-only guided thumbnails are present.
The independent study contains at least three forms or areas and names an intended focal point.
At least two hierarchy variables are identified in the learner's own work.
One intermediate state, one visual-path check, and one revision decision are documented.
Reflection and critique cite observable features; critique may be entirely private.
legitimate_variation: Any subject, abstraction, medium, format, palette, mood, style, or orientation may meet the target.
A small, large, central, edge-adjacent, isolated, repeated, detailed, or directional element may serve as the focal point when evidence supports the learner's stated intent.
The path may be steep, subtle, circular, interrupted, or intentionally ambiguous when the learner states that intention and cites observable evidence.
A learner may keep a critiqued choice, revise it, or revise the stated intent; the reasoning and evidence are scored, not agreement with the reviewer.
Difference from the Academy model is never an error and resemblance to it earns no extra credit.

rubric.exceeds: All five evidence groups are present: guided pair, original three-form study with named focal point, two named variables, preserved intermediate state plus path check and revision decision, and evidence-based reflection and critique.
rubric.meets: All required evidence is present; one record may be brief, but the guided pair, original study, two variables, intermediate state, path check, revision decision, reflection, and critique can each be located.
rubric.developing: The independent visual study is present, but one or two required evidence parts are missing or cannot be located, such as the intermediate state, path check, revision decision, reflection, or critique.
rubric.beginning: The submitted evidence does not yet include an independent three-form visual study with a named focal point, or several required process parts are absent.

rubric.exceeds: At least two hierarchy variables work together to establish the intended first stop and a readable later route; the learner precisely locates the strongest relationships and explains a meaningful tradeoff.
rubric.meets: At least two named variables create observable emphasis related to the intended focal point, and the learner cites where the eye or hand moves next using evidence from the work.
rubric.developing: Hierarchy variables are attempted, but the stated route and the observable relationships only partly align, or the explanation names variables without locating their effect in the work.
rubric.beginning: The work or explanation does not yet show a testable intended order of attention. This is a signal for focused reteaching, not a judgment about style or ability.

rubric.exceeds: The learner makes a coherent, evidence-supported case for the chosen hierarchy and recognizes another defensible reading or a deliberate ambiguity without treating it as failure.
rubric.meets: The learner states the intended order and connects specific value, scale, placement, isolation, repetition, edge, or direction evidence to that intention.
rubric.developing: The intended order is stated, but several claims rely on preference or general praise instead of observable evidence from specific locations.
rubric.beginning: The response does not yet state an intention or connect a reading to observable evidence; no particular style, subject, mood, or arrangement is required.

rubric.exceeds: The intermediate state, path check, and later state show what was tested; the learner isolates a variable, evaluates its effect, and gives an evidence-based reason to revise or deliberately keep the result.
rubric.meets: The record shows an intermediate state, one criteria-based check, and a learner-chosen revision or reasoned decision to keep the work.
rubric.developing: A change is documented, but the record does not yet make clear what evidence prompted it or which hierarchy variable changed.
rubric.beginning: No intermediate state or revision decision is visible yet. Invite a small fresh test; do not direct the learner's aesthetic choice or complete the work.

scoring_judgment_guidance: Score the submitted evidence against the four focus-specific dimensions. First record objective presence without judging polish. For hierarchy, intent, and revision, cite a location or process fact from the learner's work. Do not compare the work with the model's shapes, arrangement, palette, mood, or style. If the observed path differs from the learner's first intention, accept a reasoned revision of either the work or the stated intention. A reviewer may offer options, but the learner owns the final choice. Record NOT_YET_EVIDENCED when evidence is absent; never infer talent, care, motivation, diagnosis, or character.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task on advanced composition and visual hierarchy.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.
formative_check: Ask the learner to name the intended first, second, and third stops, point to the hierarchy variables that support each move, and compare the intermediate and later state. An unexpected but evidence-supported path is valid.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: There is no fixed composition or answer. Accept multiple valid approaches when the objective evidence is present and the learner connects observable hierarchy relationships to a stated or deliberately revised intent.
mastery_rule: This MODEL_A lesson supplies formative concept evidence, not final mastery. A later lesson must show fresh independent transfer of visual hierarchy in another composition or analysis without the model in view before a mastery claim is considered.

mastery_interpretation.secure: At least 85% with accurate independent application and adequate evidence and reasoning.
mastery_interpretation.developing: 70–84% or inconsistent explanation; assign targeted review and a fresh transfer check.
mastery_interpretation.not_yet: Below 70% or a missing prerequisite; reteach the smallest gap and reassess with new evidence.
mastery_interpretation.rule: A unit score is one evidence source, not the sole basis for long-term mastery.

unit_assessment_reference.note: This sample lesson remains formative; the unit assessment is the separate summative instrument.

remediation_paths.observable_signal: Several major areas have similarly strong contrast, edge, or detail and the intended focal point is not distinct in repeated brief checks.
remediation_paths.do_not_apply_when: The learner intends distributed, ambiguous, or nonhierarchical attention and supports that intention with evidence.
remediation_paths.alternate_instruction: Convert the work into light, middle, and dark masses; keep one large value jump near the intended first stop and quiet the others.
remediation_paths.fresh_evidence: A new three-form thumbnail with different placements plus a fresh three-second visual-path check.

remediation_paths.observable_signal: Two brief checks identify a different first stop and the learner cannot locate a hierarchy variable supporting the stated focal point.
remediation_paths.do_not_apply_when: The learner adopts the observed route as a deliberate, evidence-supported intention.
remediation_paths.alternate_instruction: Compare the intended focal point with one competing area and change exactly one of value, scale, isolation, edge, or direction on a separate scrap study.
remediation_paths.fresh_evidence: A new full thumbnail without the model in view plus a fresh visual-path check.

remediation_plan: Use remediation only for a named observable mismatch and never for a stylistic difference. If several areas compete against the learner's stated intent, use the three-value map, a separate supported thumbnail, and a fresh three-second check. If another area arrives first, compare only that area and the intended focal point, change one variable on scrap paper, then retry with a new arrangement. If the route is clear but differs from the Academy model—or if the learner deliberately supports an ambiguous or distributed hierarchy—no correction is warranted. The earlier attempt stays in the process record and carries no penalty.
extension_plan: Optionally create a second composition with the same forms and a different intended focal point. Change two hierarchy variables, compare the paths, and explain the tradeoff. Extension is never required for full credit or assigned as a penalty.
accommodation_note: Access supports may change format, pacing, setting, tool, size, contrast, or response mode while preserving the visual relationship being assessed. A tactile arrangement can provide equal evidence; prose alone cannot claim visual-making evidence.
accessibility_options: Use enlarged, high-contrast, raised-line, cut-paper, tactile, or accessible digital forms while keeping the hierarchy target unchanged.
Use relative size, spacing, texture, and touch order so colour perception never carries a criterion by itself.
Accept typed, handwritten, dictated, labelled, tactile, or adult-verified process evidence; no learner image, voice, or video is required.
Allow breaks, extended time, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting without lowering a rubric level.
task_accessibility_provisions: The required SVG includes high-contrast forms, pattern as well as value differences, descriptive title and alternative text, and a complete adjacent verbal description.
The tactile route uses three raised or cut-paper forms plus string; relative size, texture, spacing, and touch order preserve the hierarchy relationship.
A trusted adult may verify the physical artwork without photographing the learner or the home.
parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the target, completion state, evidence types, rubric levels with cited reasons, and next instructional step. Do not expose private reflection text, raw learner media, diagnosis language, or comparison with other children.

source_integrity.note: The required Three Stops SVG is committed at the package's declared locator, is Manuel Academy original under CC BY 4.0, and has embedded title/description plus verbal and tactile parallels. No external source is needed.

safety_and_privacy.note: Pencil and scrap paper are sufficient. No public display, learner photograph, camera, voice recording, account, outside search, paid tool, or specialized material is required. Private self-critique receives full credit.

standards: Michigan Arts Education Standards: Visual Arts — Creating
